introduction: Vienna's Duke leaves Angelo in charge of a city where strict laws have long gone unenforced. Angelo's reputation for self-control seems to promise a new seriousness, but the first exemplary sentence forces questions about mercy, desire, and the people who exercise judgment. Claudio's sister Isabella, preparing to enter a convent, must plead for his life before a deputy whose authority makes him difficult to challenge. Meanwhile the Duke observes his own experiment from within a friar's disguise.

fullSynopsis.text: The Duke delegates his authority to Angelo, assisted by Escalus, and pretends to leave Vienna. He actually obtains a friar's habit so that he can watch how Angelo governs and enforce neglected laws without himself appearing responsible for the sudden severity. Angelo sentences Claudio to death for making Juliet pregnant before their marriage has received its public formalities. A crackdown also threatens the city's brothels and brings their workers before the law. Lucio carries Claudio's appeal to Isabella, his sister, who has not yet taken her vows, and persuades her to seek Angelo's mercy.

Escalus urges moderation, but Angelo insists that visible offenses must be punished and that he too should die if guilty of the same fault. Isabella's first petition becomes an eloquent defense of mercy and a challenge to the deputy's use of power. It also awakens desire in him. On her return he makes the bargain explicit: he will save Claudio if she gives him her body. When she threatens exposure, he relies on his reputation and office to outweigh her testimony. Isabella refuses and goes to prepare Claudio for death, believing that he will prefer honor to survival bought through her sexual submission.

Claudio initially rejects the price but then, terrified of death, begs Isabella to save him. She condemns him and refuses. The disguised Duke has overheard them. He falsely tells Claudio that Angelo merely tested Isabella, then proposes another course to her: Mariana, whom Angelo abandoned after the loss of her dowry, will take Isabella's place in the dark encounter. The Duke presents the prior marriage contract as justification for the substitution and a means of restoring Mariana while protecting Isabella and saving Claudio. Meanwhile Pompey and Mistress Overdone are imprisoned, and Lucio unknowingly slanders the Duke to his face. Overdone reports that Lucio has also deserted a woman and child.

Mariana agrees to the substitution. Angelo believes he has possessed Isabella, yet orders Claudio executed earlier and demands his head, fearing future revenge. The Duke persuades the Provost to postpone Claudio's death and send Barnardine's head instead. Barnardine refuses to be executed while unprepared, forcing another change. A pirate, Ragozine, has died naturally and resembles Claudio; his head is sent, while both living prisoners are hidden. The Duke deliberately lets Isabella believe her brother has been killed and directs her to accuse Angelo publicly on his return. Mariana and Friar Peter prepare to support the carefully staged complaint.

At the city gate the Duke initially pretends to disbelieve Isabella, who follows his instructions by claiming she yielded to Angelo. Mariana reveals that she supplied Isabella's place. Angelo calls their testimony a conspiracy, and the Duke withdraws before returning as the friar to challenge the proceedings. Lucio repeats his slanders and pulls away the hood, exposing the Duke himself. Confronted with this witness, Angelo confesses and asks for death. The Duke orders him to marry Mariana, then condemns him to the punishment he supposedly inflicted on Claudio. Mariana pleads for him, and Isabella joins her, still believing her own brother dead.

The Provost produces Barnardine, Claudio, and Juliet. Claudio's survival ends the threat against Angelo, and the Duke pardons him, requiring him to cherish Mariana. Barnardine also receives mercy. Lucio is ordered to marry the woman he made pregnant; the Duke remits the additional whipping and hanging he first pronounced, although Lucio treats the marriage itself as punishment. Claudio is directed to restore Juliet, and the Provost is promised better employment. The Duke asks Isabella to marry him and renews his proposal at the close, but she gives no spoken answer. He leads the company toward the palace with remaining explanations still to come.

acts.label: ACT I
acts.summary: The Duke appoints Angelo to exercise his full authority in Vienna, with Escalus as assistant, and departs without public ceremony. Claudio is arrested under revived laws against sexual relations outside formal marriage: Juliet is pregnant, though he explains that they have a true private contract and postponed public arrangements over her dowry. The same enforcement threatens the suburban brothels, alarming Mistress Overdone and Pompey. Claudio sends Lucio to ask Isabella, a novice at a convent, to plead for him. At the monastery the Duke reveals that he intends to remain disguised as a friar, observing Angelo and allowing another man to enforce laws his own leniency left idle. Lucio reaches Isabella and persuades her to leave temporarily to seek mercy.

acts.label: ACT II
acts.summary: Angelo rejects Escalus's plea for Claudio and orders execution, declaring that the same fault should bring the same judgment on himself. Elbow's confused accusations and Pompey's evasive answers expose another difficulty in governing vice; Escalus dismisses Froth and warns Pompey against continuing his trade. Isabella, prompted by Lucio, argues that mercy becomes authority and that judges should examine their own frailty. Angelo asks her to return, privately recognizing his desire. The disguised Duke visits pregnant Juliet and discusses repentance. At the second interview Angelo demands Isabella's body as the price of Claudio's life. He threatens her brother with suffering and insists his public credit will defeat her accusation. Isabella refuses and resolves to tell Claudio what his pardon would cost.

acts.label: ACT III
acts.summary: The Duke prepares Claudio for death before overhearing Isabella explain Angelo's demand. Claudio first rejects it, then begs her to consent as fear overcomes him; Isabella angrily refuses. The Duke falsely tells Claudio that Angelo was testing her, then privately proposes substituting Mariana, Angelo's abandoned betrothed, at the night meeting. He argues that their earlier contract makes the encounter a restoration rather than dishonor, and Isabella accepts the plan. In the streets Pompey goes to prison while Lucio declines to bail him. Lucio then slanders the absent Duke to the man concealed in the friar's habit. Mistress Overdone, also committed to prison, reports Lucio's broken promise to a mother of his child. Escalus remains troubled by Claudio's sentence, and the Duke prepares his intervention.

acts.label: ACT IV
acts.summary: A song of broken love introduces Mariana, who agrees to enter Angelo's garden-house in Isabella's place. At the prison Pompey becomes the executioner's assistant. Contrary to the Duke's hope of pardon, Angelo accelerates Claudio's death and demands his head. The Duke secures the Provost's cooperation in substituting Barnardine, but that prisoner refuses to die unprepared. Ragozine's natural death supplies a head resembling Claudio's, and both threatened prisoners are hidden. The Duke conceals Claudio's survival from Isabella to make a later revelation more powerful. He directs her public accusation, arranges his official return, and prepares Friar Peter to guide the women. Angelo regrets ordering the death but still relies on his authority and Isabella's presumed shame to protect him.

acts.label: ACT V
acts.summary: The Duke stages a public hearing, first rejecting Isabella's complaint and then hearing Mariana's account of the substitution. Returning as the friar, he is unhooded by Lucio and recognized. Angelo confesses, marries Mariana on command, and faces a death sentence for Claudio's supposed execution. Mariana's plea draws Isabella into asking mercy for the man she believes killed her brother. The Provost then reveals Claudio alive; the Duke pardons him, Angelo, and Barnardine. Lucio must marry the woman he wronged, while his threatened corporal and capital punishments are remitted. Claudio is told to make restitution to Juliet, and the Provost is promised a better post. The Duke proposes marriage to Isabella, who does not answer in the text, and invites everyone to the palace.
